steps.content: [The Great Expo Entrance]
In a secluded corner of the plaza, Thalia stretches her arms and rubs her stiff shoulders.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Yawn... Day 9! Just hang in there, it's almost over!

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: The viewer count... still a few more to go. Should I switch to Parfait's dinner party tomorrow, or stick with the closing ceremony?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Looks like the Outland Expo just can't keep up with Nirvana's market boom for viewer attention... I'll need something more viral to get the sales going... Huh?
As she murmurs, Thalia's sharp gaze snaps to a sudden commotion in the plaza. Muscle memory takes over—her fingers flick the camera on before she even thinks.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: What's going on over there?
[Scene Change]
An Outlander stumbles into the center of the plaza, breathless and disheveled. The crowd recoils, their instinctive retreat carving an accidental stage around her.

Her chest heaves in raging emotions, her teeth gritted as she fights for control. Bloodshot eyes rake the onlookers—accusing, desperate. Finally, Sibilla speaks, trembling as she straightens up under the weight of countless stares. She forces the Disian words out with her best efforts, each syllable deliberate, yet some still twist defiantly on her tongue.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: I am... Sibilla, an inspector of Furor. I've come to expose Fraser's lies... and denounce their crimes!
However, her words hang in the air, met first with a heavy silence, then scattered murmurs rippling through the crowd.

steps.speaker: Passerby
steps.content: Furor? What place is that? Never even heard of it.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Fraser has been lying from the start. The Aurum Secretum mining sites must be built in the most dangerous calamity zones, but instead of taking the risks themselves, they tricked my people into going in their place.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: We built mining sites and research facilities, protecting their researchers, even though we had no Hypercubes to protect ourselves. We trusted them. But Fraser never warned us that the Aurum Secretum would have devastating effects. The Furorians' bodies slowly deteriorated, our numbers dwindling until, in the end, people died still believing in them.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: But that's not all. Fraser has taken complete control over Hypercube trade, stockpiled resources, and extorted every village—all while lying to our faces and pinning the blame on DisCity. They've been fueling hatred in the Farland Alliance, turning people against DisCity. Because the more we despise them, the more we depend on Fraser, and the tighter their grip on us becomes.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: There have also been forbidden experiments and brainwashed extremists. They take our children. They hunt down anyone who knows too much. I barely escaped... and I'm the only one who made it here. All I want is to tell you the truth, and...

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Please, help us, stop those people! Please save Furor!

steps.speaker: Passerby A
steps.content: Don't touch me! You dirty hag... What gibberish are you speaking?
She's shoved to the ground, then a shoe slams into her side, deliberate and cruel.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: ...Huh?
Sibilla stumbles unsteadily to her feet. She wonders if she didn't explain herself properly. Was something unclear? Was her accent too heavy? Her vision blurs as her head begins to buzz.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: ...Was I unclear somehow...? Th-then I'll say it one more time...
This time, the audience offers their answer before she makes a sound.

steps.speaker: Passerby B
steps.content: An Outlander? Heh... What a filthy beggar.
The crowd stirs back to life. Most have already pieced together the situation, drawn their conclusions, and moved on. They quicken their steps as they pass Sibilla, veering wide to avoid her.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Ah... no... I'm not lying, please... just listen to me...

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Please help us. I don't want money... Just help me spread the word, or even just telling more people would help...
Someone has noticed her at last. Several cameras now point in her direction.

steps.speaker: Passerby B
steps.content: Pfft, why'd you stop the act? At least be professional with your sob story. Go on, keep it up.

steps.speaker: Passerby B
steps.content: You want eyes on you? At least have a pretty face. Pathetic. We've seen dozens like you this week.
These hecklers attract attention better than she does. She's quickly becoming nothing but a public spectacle. How can she make them understand? How can she make them care?
...Would it draw more attention if those Fraser people came to kill her? Sibilla trembles as she pushes herself upright, then erupts into frantic shouts.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: You Campbells!! Haven't you been trying to kill me all along? Come on then! I'm right here! Come and kill me!!

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Let everyone see what you've done to Furor! What you've done to us!! Come on, show yourselves!!
She screams until her voice grows hoarse, but no one responds.

Sibilla realizes, with a sinking clarity, why no one has tried to kill her all this time. Fraser already knows the truth—she doesn't need to be silenced because no one would ever listen. Not DisCity, not Fraser, not a soul.

Just as despair threatens to swallow her whole, someone roughly grabs her by the shoulder. Has someone finally heard her? Her gaze snaps up to a uniformed figure. A public official? Has someone actually taken her seriously?!

Sibilla's fingers twist into the fabric of the stranger's uniform, a silent plea. The answer comes not in words, but in a crushing blow to her skull. Pain erupts, spinning the world into a blur. Through the dizzying haze, she barely catches the sheriff's face—his features twisted in pure disgust.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Quiet! This is the Great Expo! You've already been reported for causing a disturbance and spreading panic. Still looking for trouble? Move it!
Sibilla is yanked up by her collar and, still dazed from the blow, dragged across the plaza. The sheriff shoves her into the waiting transport and slams the door shut.
From a safe distance, Thalia watches in silence, her camera heavy in her grip. The Outlander's desperation coils around her, awakening a long-dormant compassion.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Sigh...

Thalia sighs softly, subtly bending the crowd's focus toward Sibilla with her power. More and more people at the scene start to notice what's happening, yet the viewership of her stream stubbornly refuses to climb.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: If they're throttling the stream, there's nothing more I can do for you.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Poor thing... but playing the victim card just doesn't work in DisCity.
She ends her stream and opens her terminal, thinking about who she could contact to help take the Outlander away, only to discover Sibilla is already gone.

By the time Sibilla regains her senses, the vehicle has already driven far from the plaza. She staggers upright and hurls herself toward the narrow barred window that cages her from the driver's compartment. Her voice tears through the iron grate.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: ...Are you arresting me? That's great! Thank you for taking me in. Just get me to that Bureau, let me see that person. I'll do anything!

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Can you understand what I'm saying? I—

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Screw off! Who's got time for beggar trash like you?

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: They hold one Great Expo and thousands of filthy Outland beggars show up. The Outland Affairs Bureau should just drag the lot of you out to WhiteSands and let the worms feast!

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Open your mouth again and I'll shoot you—Ugh!
His verbal abuse is cut short by a violent crash as a tremendous force slams directly into the driver's side, sending the entire vehicle flying through the air.

Inside the twisted carcass of the ruptured vehicle, the sheriff's head lolls to one side, lifeless. An ominous burning stench begins to flood the car as Sibilla struggles to claw her way across the floor, desperately reaching her hand toward the outside.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Cough...
In the crimson dusk, she spots two familiar silhouettes.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Arienna... Adriel...
Just as how they saved her back then, the two crouch down and reach toward Sibilla—then drive a knife through the back of her hand.

steps.speaker: Arienna
steps.content: ...So naive, Sibilla. Did you really think they'd help? DisCity doesn't care. They don't understand our suffering—they can't even imagine it.

steps.speaker: Arienna
steps.content: People living in a different world simply cannot see our pain.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: ...I know. I knew it all along...

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: When I was with them, I realized... we're from completely different worlds...
She loves that street they call a "slum." It has electricity, running water, and beds where sleep comes soundly behind a locked door.
No calamity alarms shatter the night. No families flee in panic, leaving lifetimes of labor behind.
When Harry felt ashamed of the "cheap candy" he offered, Sibilla didn't dare tell him... that such treats were most treasured back in her homeland.

In the Outlands, only the bravest and most diligent children can earn such rare, sweet rewards. The joy on the children's faces as they cradle candy in their palms is Sibilla's most cherished memory. Yet here, such things are apparently embarrassing to offer.

Parfait must hide her origins. DisCity sneers at "drifters" from the slums. People are embarrassed to offer cheap candy to guests. So... who would spare a second glance at someone as poor as her? Is it foolish to keep pursuing that Chief, hoping against hope?

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Fraser... cares even less if we live or die.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: So do you.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: I've reached out to everyone I could find, and this isn't the first time I've been rejected...

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: If the people of DisCity won't help me, then I'll find someone who will, anywhere I have to go. It doesn't matter how many times I get turned away. I won't stop until someone finally listens... until someone actually cares enough to do something.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: I won't give up. If Fraser wants to shut me up, they'll have to kill me first. I'm not stopping.

steps.speaker: Arienna
steps.content: ...I see.
Arienna stands up and brings her weapon to Sibilla's throat.

steps.speaker: Arienna
steps.content: Even if Fraser says you're worthless... even if part of me wishes you could live... you're too dangerous. You have to go.

steps.speaker: Arienna
steps.content: We really are the same, you and us. Neither of us has a choice.
